title: One Christ, both God and man, not divided
english: He said to the disciples, “Do not call anyone on earth ‘teacher,’ for you have one guide, the Christ” (Matthew 23:8). For when he gave this command to the apostles, he was not separating his own divinity from the visible body. Nor when he bore witness that he himself was the Christ was he dividing soul and flesh in that way, since he is both God and man at once—seen as a slave and known as Lord. orientation: Cyril is opening his second book against Theodore by quoting Christ's saying to the disciples about the one teacher and explaining that this does not separate Christ's divinity from his visible body.
